coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia's 2007 LSU Tigers football team page "Coaching staff" table (10 on-field coaches + Moffitt + 2 GAs). (2) The 2007 LSU Football Media Guide, scanned on archive.org (item lsu-football-2007-media-guide-c). Nearly every quote below is copied verbatim from that item's machine-readable OCR text file at https://archive.org/download/lsu-football-2007-media-guide-c/LSU%20Football%202007%20Media%20Guide%20%28C%29_djvu.txt — the quotes will match that URL, not the PDF. (3) Individual Wikipedia biographies for corroborating prose.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO. The Wayback Machine's replay service (web.archive.org/web/...) returned HTTP 503 "No server is available to handle this request" on every attempt from this environment, and WebFetch refuses that host outright, so I could NOT consult the archived lsusports.net staff directory near the title date (step 2 of the requested source order). The archive.org-hosted media guide substituted for it. The WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted before I began, so no contemporary news articles (hire announcements, championship coverage) could be searched; step 4 is entirely unrepresented.

TIMING CAVEAT (important for the ring rule). The media guide is a PRESEASON document published in August 2007. It documents the staff as constituted at the start of the season, NOT as verified on January 7, 2008. I found no evidence of any mid-season departure among these 38 people, but I also could not positively confirm each support-staff member was still employed at the BCS title game. The one well-known complication is Bo Pelini, who accepted the Nebraska head-coaching job in December 2007 yet remained LSU's defensive coordinator through the championship game (noted on his row).

OCR CAVEATS. The archive.org text is uncorrected OCR of a two-column scanned page. Several quotes therefore contain visible OCR artifacts that I have preserved exactly rather than cleaning up: "SharonMangum" (run-together), "1oth" for 10th, "1lth" for 11th, "Ist" for 1st, and stray schedule text bleeding into staff rows. On the "Football Support Staff" photo-grid page (guide p. 110), each person's name and title fall on separate OCR lines, so for those twelve people I supply the name as one quote and the title as a second quote from the same URL, with a note — the two are not contiguous in the text and must not be matched as a single string.

TIERS I RECOVERED: head coach (1), on-field assistants (9 — the full NCAA-maximum complement, so this tier is complete), strength and conditioning (6), graduate assistants (2), operations/personnel/recruiting (11), medical/athletic training (3), equipment (4), video (2). Total 38.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER. (a) ANALYSTS and QUALITY CONTROL: no such titles existed in LSU's documented 2007 structure; zero rows. The closest analogues are the three "Administrative Intern" positions (Farrell, Papuchis, Wozniak), which I categorized as ops rather than guess. (b) GRADUATE ASSISTANTS are almost certainly undercounted. The media guide does not list football GAs by name at all; my two rows come solely from Wikipedia. Note the conflict on Mike Ekeler: Wikipedia documents him as a graduate assistant 2005–2007, while the 2007 media guide lists him under "Assistant Strength Coach" — the era's common title workaround. Glen Elarbee appears in Wikipedia but nowhere in the media guide. A typical 2007 SEC staff carried more GAs than two; I did not invent them. (c) TEAM PHYSICIANS / ORTHOPEDIC SURGEONS: the football media guide names none. (Dr. James Andrews appears in the guide only as a distinguished LSU alumnus, not as staff, so I excluded him.) (d) STUDENT and PART-TIME staff: the guide states the video department alone "oversees a staff of eight people... one full-time assistant, one graduate assistant and six student assistants," and that athletic training runs "a staff of six full-time trainers and 10 graduate assistants" department-wide — none of these individuals are named, and only the three trainers assigned to football are identified. Equipment student managers likewise unnamed. (e) ACADEMIC SUPPORT: the guide's academic-center staff is department-wide across 20 sports and not separable into football-specific personnel, so I included none. (f) RECRUITING/PERSONNEL beyond the four named administrators is not documented.

Every row has a real, verifiable source. Nothing was padded.
